page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is an entry-tier memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with two threads on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor capable of reaching up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache pool. Hardware capability includes advanced instruction sets such as Intel AMX tile and int8 alongside AVX-512 extensions for specialized vector and matrix execution. System memory is sized at 16 GB, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, coupled with 118 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for temporary workloads without relying on external block storage.

Empirical benchmark results reflect the specific architectural configuration of this two-vCPU instance. Single-core processing demonstrates moderate capability, recording a stress-ng score of 2215.58 in the middle tier. However, overall multi-core computational throughput is bounded by the single-core two-thread boundary, resulting in a lower stress-ng multi-core mark of 2263.98 and a PassMark CPU score of 4263.53. Memory subsystem benchmarks show an average PassMark memory score of 1927.71 and 168.1 GB/sec cached small-block read speeds, though larger uncached memory transfers decline to 22.92 GB/sec read and 12.15 GB/sec write. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET operations reached 4.01 million operations per second, and static web serving sustained 4.95 GB/sec throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the E2ds_v7 avoids the expenditure of multi-core configurations when the operational bottleneck is RAM capacity or local disk latency. The inclusion of bundled NVMe storage provides rapid scratch space without attaching premium external volumes, though compute-bound scaling is strictly limited by the single physical core. This profile makes Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 best suited for distributed caching layers, Redis nodes, small relational or document databases, lightweight ETL staging, and memory-sensitive containerized services.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is an entry-tier memory-optimized instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C core operating up to 4.2 GHz. The instance delivers 16 GB of system RAM, maintaining a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, alongside a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. Advanced hardware extensions are present, including Intel AMX and AVX-512 for accelerated matrix and vector calculations. Benchmark profiles indicate solid single-core throughput with an average stress-ng score of 2215.58, though aggregate multi-threaded compute remains constrained by the dual-vCPU topology. Memory-intensive execution is supported by average PassMark memory scores and 4.01 million Redis SET operations per second, while large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks exhibit lower uncached throughput. The integrated local NVMe drive offers low-latency temporary storage, avoiding network-attached storage latency for ephemeral data. Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is appropriately tailored for small in-memory caching layers, Redis instances, lightweight database engines, and microservices requiring elevated RAM relative to processing cores.
